fidelity: F2a — Thevenin Equivalent-Circuit Model (1-RC / 2-RC) with Coulomb-counted SOC and Thermal ODE
source: Berndt (2003) Maintenance-Free Batteries, Wiley; Shepherd (1965) J. Electrochem. Soc. 112, 657; Thomas & Newman (2003) J. Electrochem. Soc. 150, A176; Plett (2015) Battery Management Systems Vol.2, Artech House; Hu et al. (2012) J. Power Sources 198, 359 (ECM comparison)

unit.name: Standard NiCd D-cell (sintered plate) — Thevenin ECM

capacity_ref.note: Nominal capacity at T_ref (C/5 rate). Berndt (2003)

R0_ref.note: Series ohmic resistance at T_ref. Very low for NiCd (sintered plates, KOH electrolyte). Berndt (2003)

C1_ref.note: First RC capacitance — fast double-layer/charge-transfer; tau1 = R1*C1 ~ 9 s

C2_ref.note: Second RC capacitance — slow diffusion; tau2 = R2*C2 ~ 120 s

ocv_a0.note: OCV(SOC) polynomial coeff a0 (reused from EC030 F1b)

ocv_a5.note: OCV(SOC) coeff a5 — gives flat ~1.2-1.25 V plateau

E_a.note: Arrhenius activation energy for resistances. Low for aqueous KOH. Berndt (2003); Plett (2015)

dOCV_dT.note: Entropic coefficient ~ -0.60 mV/K. NiOOH+H2O+e- -> Ni(OH)2+OH- has large negative entropy -> strong discharge heating. Thomas & Newman (2003)

coulombic_eff.note: NiCd charge acceptance efficiency ~85-92% (gassing/side reactions on charge). Berndt (2003). Discharge eff ~1.0

hA_cell.note: Convective heat-transfer coeff * surface area to ambient (natural convection)

current_A.note: Negative=charge, Positive=discharge; NiCd tolerates very high rates

temperature.note: -30 to 60 degC; NiCd excels at low T
